To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the subretinal detachment expands in the first three days following subretinal injection and that the lateral spread of GFP expression is due to this expansion and not to the diffusion of vector beyond the subretinall bleb.

there is lateral spread of transduction beyond the subretinall bleb in normal dogs following AAV-mediated subretinal injection and that this spread is due to post injection expansion of the sub-retinal bleb.
there is lateral spread of transgenic gene expression following subretinal injection of AAV vectors in dogs and this is related to the extent of retinal detachment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lateral spread of gene expression following subretinal injection of gene therapy vectors.
the evaluation of the lateral spread and its mechanism in the retina of normal dogs after subretinal injection of three different AAV serotypes (AAV2, 2/5 and 2/8).
the evaluation of the lateral spread and the potential of the AAV vectors to induce retinal detachment in dogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was a very slight extension (less than 1 mm) of GFP expression beyond that of the final subretinal blebs in some eyes.
there is no lateral spread of transgenic protein expression beyond the initial subretinal blebs in normal dogs.
there is no evidence of any lateral spread of transgenic expression beyond the sub-retinal bleb boundary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lateral spread of gene expression is a consequence of the subretinally induced retinal detachment and is not a property of the vector.
the lateral spread of the bleb and GFP expression is not a desirable feature of subretinal AAV-mediated gene therapy in dogs.
the lateral spread of the bleb is the main determinant of lateral spread of transduction, and the bleb is not static, but can change over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral spread of gene expression beyond the sub-retinal bleb is likely due to post-injection spread and not to the vector itself.

subretinal injections in dogs can lead to a transient retinal detachment which expands over time and that the lateral spread of the retinotomy can lead to a lateral spread of the transgene expression.
the lateral spread of the subretinall bleb and the retinal detachment is the main cause for the spread of the transgene expression.
